summary: Verified bug fix for pending-order auto-cleanup. Root cause was case mismatch: orders route inserts status='Pending' (capital) but cleanup query filtered status='pending' (lowercase), so nothing ever matched. Fix in /app/backend/order_cleanup.py now uses $in: ['Pending','pending']. Confirmed via direct DB seed + direct invocation of cleanup_old_pending_orders(): both old 'Pending' and 'pending' orders were deleted, fresh Pending order kept, and old 'Completed'/'Confirmed'/'cancelled' orders were preserved. Supervisor backend logs also show '✅ Order cleanup background task started (interval=5min, ttl=30min)' and multiple '🗑️ Auto-deleted N pending orders older than 30 minutes' entries confirming the periodic task runs on server boot.

minor.issue: If cleanup raises an exception, the loop only logs and immediately sleeps 5 min - fine. However on first-time schedule, there's no initial delay; harmless but worth noting.
Duplicate class definitions of OrderItem and CreateOrderRequest (lines 22-41 and 72-88) - dead code, second overrides first. Code hygiene issue, not functional.

action_items: (Optional cleanup) Remove duplicate OrderItem / CreateOrderRequest class definitions in /app/backend/routes/orders.py (lines 22-41 vs 72-88).
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and minimal: $in match covers historic lowercase data plus current 'Pending' writes.
created_at is stored as ISO 8601 UTC string; $lt with ISO cutoff string works because ISO 8601 sorts lexicographically for same-format timestamps. Good.

run_cleanup_task uses a bare `while True` with 5-min sleep and per-iteration client open/close in cleanup_old_pending_orders. Acceptable but could reuse the shared motor client (database.db) to avoid churn.
server.py properly schedules the task via asyncio.create_task on startup event. Confirmed running in supervisor logs.
Duplicate Pydantic models in routes/orders.py (OrderItem, CreateOrderRequest, PaymentScreenshotUpload, BulkDeleteRequest defined twice) — should be de-duplicated.
seed_data_creation: 6 TEST_-prefixed synthetic orders inserted directly into MongoDB during the test module, all cleaned up in module teardown. No residual test data.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for auto-deletion of stale Pending orders is verified. Pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_order_cleanup.py exercises both status cases + negative cases (Completed/Confirmed/cancelled preservation) + idempotency. Backend startup log confirms scheduler is registered.
rca of the issue: RCA: /app/backend/routes/orders.py::create_order sets status='Pending' (capital P) when inserting, while the original cleanup query in /app/backend/order_cleanup.py used {'status':'pending'} (lowercase). MongoDB matches are case-sensitive, so the delete_many query never matched any real order and pending orders piled up indefinitely. Reproduction: insert a doc {status:'Pending', created_at: <31min ago ISO>}; run cleanup_old_pending_orders() with old code -> doc still present. Mitigation applied: change query to {'status': {'$in': ['Pending','pending']}}. Verified via test_cleanup_deletes_old_pending_orders (both cases removed) and by observing '🗑️ Auto-deleted N pending orders' in supervisor logs post-restart. Long-term recommendation: pick one canonical case (recommend 'pending' or an enum) and migrate all existing docs, then drop the $in fallback.
